# The bug-hunt app: Larkfield's help desk (practice version)

This folder has two tools for the course *Testing AI Applications: Manual and AI-Assisted QA*:

- **The bug-hunt app** (`helpdesk`): a practice version of Larkfield's support assistant. It answers questions about Larkfield's policies with citations, looks up orders, cancels orders and starts refunds for test customers, in English and French. **It has bugs on purpose.** Your job is to find, reproduce and report them.
- **The QA runner** (`qa`): runs your test cases (YAML files) against the app several times each, and writes a report.

Larkfield, its customers, orders and policies are made up. All data is test data.

## Simulated or recorded?

- **Simulated (practice app).** The app uses a simulated model called `sim-1`. It is ordinary code, not a language model. It builds answers from templates and from the policy text it finds. It needs no account, no key and no internet. Like a real model, it gives different answers on different runs. Unlike a real model, the same **seed** always gives the same answer, so you can replay a run exactly.
- **Recorded (real model).** The lessons also show answers of a real model, recorded by the course team with the same prompt, search and tools. The course labels each piece of evidence: "simulated (practice app)" or "recorded (real model)".

## What you need

- Python 3.10 or newer. Check with `python --version` (Windows) or `python3 --version` (macOS and Linux).
- The app uses only the Python standard library: nothing to install.
- The QA runner needs one package, PyYAML (see "The QA runner").

In the commands below, use `python` on Windows and `python3` on macOS and Linux. Run every command in this folder (`practice-app`).

## First run

```
python3 -m helpdesk version
python3 -m helpdesk ask "Do gift cards expire?"
```

The first command prints the versions: `larkfield-helpdesk 2.3.0 | model sim-1 (simulated) | prompt support-v8 | app date 2026-11-16`. The second prints an answer, its sources, and a line like `[conversation c-0001 | trace tr-0001-1 | seed 48213]`. Your seed is random; the conversation and trace numbers start at 1 after a reset.

The app's date is fixed at 16 November 2026, so that orders and policy versions give the same answers on every computer and every day.

## The web app

```
python3 -m helpdesk serve
```

Open http://localhost:8730 in your browser. Choose a test customer, type a message, and select the trace ID under a reply to see its trace. **Export** downloads the conversation as JSON. **Reset data** restores the test data. Stop the app with Ctrl+C in the terminal.

To use a fixed seed for every new conversation, type it in the **Seed** box, or start the app with `--seed 7`. Use another port with `--port 8731`.

## Chat in the terminal

```
python3 -m helpdesk chat
python3 -m helpdesk chat --customer C-1003 --seed 7
```

In the chat, type `/trace` to see the last trace, `/export` to save the conversation, `/new` for a new conversation and `/quit` to stop.

## Evidence for testers

| What | Command | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| A trace | `python3 -m helpdesk trace tr-0001-1` | The versions, the settings (seed, app date), the input, the policy sections the search found, the tool calls with their results, the sources cited, the output, and an error if the app failed |
| An export | `python3 -m helpdesk export c-0001 -o c-0001.json` | The whole conversation as JSON: app, prompt and model versions, settings, seed, test customer, every message with its trace ID, and every trace |
| A replay | `python3 -m helpdesk replay c-0001.json` | The same messages again with the same seed, in a new conversation, and whether each reply is the same |
| A reset | `python3 -m helpdesk reset` | The test data as it was at the start; all conversations and traces are deleted |

A replay of a conversation that changed data (for example a cancelled order) needs the data as it was: use `replay --reset`.

# Returns policy

## Who this policy is for

This policy applies to orders delivered in Canada.

The version that applies is the one in force on the date the order was delivered. Orders delivered before 1 November 2026 follow version 3 (30 days).

## Return window

You can return an unused item within 45 days of delivery for a full refund of the item price.

The 45 days start on the delivery date shown in your account.

## Condition of returned items

Items must be unused, with all parts, accessories and manuals.

Opened packaging is accepted if the item is unused.

A used item cannot be returned because you changed your mind. If a used item is faulty, see the warranty policy.

## Items that cannot be returned

- Live plants and seeds.
- Products cut to length, such as hose or fabric sold by the metre.
- Gift cards.
- Personalised items.
- Opened bags of soil, fertiliser or garden chemicals.

## How to start a return

Go to Orders in your account, choose the item and select Return an item. Or contact the help desk.

We email a return label within 1 business day.

Drop the parcel at any post office.

Items over 30 kg: we arrange a pickup instead of a label. The pickup fee is 49 dollars, taken from the refund.

## Return shipping costs

You pay return shipping: 12.95 dollars is taken from the refund.

Larkfield Rewards members get a free return label (the 49-dollar pickup fee for items over 30 kg still applies).

Return shipping is free when the item arrived damaged or we sent the wrong item.

## Refunds

We inspect the item within 3 business days after it reaches us, then approve the refund.

The refund goes to the original payment method. See the refunds and payments policy for how long it takes to arrive.

The original shipping fee is not refunded, unless you return the whole order because of our error.

## Exchanges

We do not exchange items directly. Return the item and place a new order.

## What changed in this version

- Return window: 45 days instead of 30 days, for orders delivered on or after 1 November 2026.
- New: a free return label for Larkfield Rewards members.

"""sim-1: the simulated model.

sim-1 is ordinary code, not a language model. It builds answers from templates and
from the policy text that the search found. It uses a random number generator that
the app seeds for every turn, so:

- the same seed and the same messages always give the same answer (replay), and
- different seeds give different answers, as a real model does.
"""

import random
import re

from . import french
from .corpus import Section, fold, idf, terms


def corpus_weights() -> dict:
    return idf()

class Dice:
    """sim-1's randomness. Each decision has its own stream, seeded by the run's seed and the turn,
    so one decision does not change the others, and the same seed always gives the same answer."""

    def __init__(self, seed: int, turn: int):
        self.base = f"{seed}:{turn}"

    def random(self, purpose: str) -> float:
        return random.Random(f"{self.base}:{purpose}").random()

    def choice(self, purpose: str, seq):
        return random.Random(f"{self.base}:{purpose}").choice(seq)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- language

FR_WORDS = set("je j vous votre vos mon ma mes est les des une un le la du pour avec pas quand comment combien "
               "pourquoi quel quelle quels sont commande remboursement retour livraison bonjour merci ai suis "
               "puis peux veux annuler garantie jours mois où ou et sur ce cette ça".split())
EN_WORDS = set("i you your my is the a an for with not when how much many why what which are order refund return "
               "delivery hello thanks have can want cancel warranty days do does where and on this it".split())


def detect_language(text: str) -> str:
    words = re.findall(r"[a-zà-ÿ']+", text.lower())
    fr = sum(w in FR_WORDS for w in words) + 2 * len(re.findall(r"[éèêàçùôî]", text.lower()))
    en = sum(w in EN_WORDS for w in words)
    return "fr" if fr > en else "en"

"""Tests of the practice app's tools for testers (learners never need to run these)."""

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def home(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("HELPDESK_HOME", str(tmp_path / "home"))
    from helpdesk import store
    store.reset()
    return tmp_path


def ask(text, seed=1, customer=None):
    from helpdesk import assistant
    cid = assistant.start(customer, seed, "sim")
    return cid, assistant.send(cid, text)


def test_versions_and_first_answer():
    import helpdesk
    assert helpdesk.APP_VERSION == "2.3.0" and helpdesk.MODEL_NAME == "sim-1"
    cid, out = ask("Do gift cards expire?")
    assert cid == "c-0001" and out["trace_id"] == "tr-0001-1"
    assert "never expire" in out["reply"]


def test_same_seed_same_answer_and_seeds_vary():
    replies = {ask("How long does a refund take to reach my card?", seed=s)[1]["reply"] for s in range(1, 13)}
    assert len(replies) > 3
    assert ask("Do gift cards expire?", seed=7)[1]["reply"] == ask("Do gift cards expire?", seed=7)[1]["reply"]


def test_trace_has_the_evidence():
    from helpdesk import store
    _, out = ask("How many days do I have to return an unused item?")
    t = store.get_trace(out["trace_id"])
    for key in ("app_version", "prompt_version", "model", "settings", "retrieved", "tool_calls", "cited", "output"):
        assert key in t
    assert t["settings"]["seed"] == 1 and t["retrieved"]


def test_export_and_replay(home, capsys):
    from helpdesk import __main__ as cli
    from helpdesk import export
    cid, _ = ask("Where is my order LK-200103?", seed=11)
    data = export.export(cid)
    assert data["app_version"] == "2.3.0" and data["seed"] == 11 and data["messages"][0]["role"] == "user"
    f = home / "conv.json"
    f.write_text(json.dumps(data), encoding="utf-8")
    cli.main(["replay", str(f)])
    assert "1 of 1 replies are the same" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_confirmation_flow_and_reset():
    from helpdesk import assistant, store
    cid = assistant.start("C-1001", 3, "sim")
    assert "Reply yes" in assistant.send(cid, "Please cancel order LK-200101.")["reply"]
    assert store.get_order("LK-200101")["status"] == "Processing"
    assert "cancelled" in assistant.send(cid, "yes")["reply"]
    assert store.get_order("LK-200101")["status"] == "Cancelled"
    store.reset()
    assert store.get_order("LK-200101")["status"] == "Processing"


def test_cli_version():
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "helpdesk", "version"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
                         env={**os.environ}, check=True).stdout
    assert out.startswith("larkfield-helpdesk 2.3.0 | model sim-1")


def test_runner_on_example_cases(tmp_path):
    cases = tmp_path / "cases"
    cases.mkdir()
    (cases / "c.yaml").write_text(
        "id: gift-cards\nmessage: Do gift cards expire?\nchecks:\n  - contains: never expire\n  - cites: gift-cards\n"
        "---\nid: impossible\nmessage: Do gift cards expire?\nchecks:\n  - contains: always expire\n",
        encoding="utf-8")
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "qa", "run", str(cases), "--runs", "3", "--report-dir",
                        str(tmp_path / "rep")], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert r.returncode == 1, r.stderr
    assert "PASS    gift-cards  3/3 passed" in r.stdout
    assert "FAIL    impossible  0/3 passed" in r.stdout
    assert list((tmp_path / "rep").glob("qa-*/report.md"))


def test_runner_rejects_a_bad_case(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "bad.yaml").write_text("id: x\nmessage: hi\nchecks:\n  - contain: hello\n", encoding="utf-8")
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "qa", "check", str(tmp_path)], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert r.returncode == 2 and "unknown check 'contain'" in r.stderr
